profiles.name: Bear Lincoln
profiles.description: Eugene Bear Lincoln, a member of the Wailacki of the Round Valley Indian Tribes, was charged with murder after an April 1995 shootout on the Round Valley Reservation near Covelo, California, in which Mendocino County Sheriff Deputy Bob Davis and Lincoln's friend Leonard Acorn Peters were killed. Maintaining that he fired in self-defense after deputies ambushed the two men, Lincoln turned himself in at the San Francisco law office of attorney Tony Serra. He was held without bail in the Mendocino County jail for two years. In 1997, after a trial that drew national attention to law-enforcement treatment of Native people in Mendocino County, a jury acquitted Lincoln of murder. He was later, in 2000, convicted of an unrelated charge of firing into reservation homes.
profiles.finding: SFGate manhunt, CTInsider surrender and Albion Monitor mirror match Bear Lincoln. MEC newsletter image captions supporters, not Lincoln; reject that image. Archive portrait follow-up remains.
profiles.rights: No image selected; original credit and rights verification pending.

profiles.name: Sundiata Jawanza
profiles.description:
Sundiata Jawanza, born Darvin Allen, has been imprisoned in the South Carolina state prison system since 1995, serving a life sentence for murder and accessory after the fact of armed robbery. He has expressed remorse for the offenses of his youth and during his three decades inside has become one of the most consequential prison-rights organizers in the United States.

He is a founder of Jailhouse Lawyers Speak, the prisoner-led network that since 2018 has organized national prison work strikes and the Free Alabama Movement-style campaigns against forced prison labor. He is Co-Chair of the National Lawyers Guild Mass Incarceration Committee and the Mass Defense Committee, and the Jailhouse Lawyer Vice President on the NLGs National Executive Committee. He is also an Imam who serves as the spiritual guide for the Muslim population in his facility, and a certified peer support specialist who teaches substance-use and mental-health classes inside.

South Carolina prison authorities have responded to his organizing by holding him in closed custody. In April 2023 he was transferred to the Turbeville Correctional Institution to complete the Addiction Treatment Unit program in support of his parole eligibility. The Jericho Movement classifies him as a politicized prisoner — a person originally incarcerated for ordinary criminal charges who has become a political prisoner through subsequent organizing inside.
profiles.finding: Jericho July-August2024 newsletter is a profile lead; NLG statement open failed with internal error. Original portrait and rights pending.

profiles.name: Peter Eamon Maguire
profiles.description: Peter Eamon Maguire, known as Eamon McGuire, was an aviation engineer and IRA activist born in County Monaghan in 1936. A separate defendant in the prosecution associated with the Boston Three, he was extradited to the United States in February 1994. He pleaded guilty to three charges connected with an IRA arms-export and anti-helicopter conspiracy and received a 70-month federal sentence on June 15, 1994. His US imprisonment included FCI Cumberland. Federal custody ended on September 29, 1997, in the year he was transferred to Ireland to finish his sentence; he was released there before Christmas. He later published the prison-written memoir Enemy of the Empire.
profiles.finding: Irish Times transfer/release coverage matches Eamon McGuire; memoir Enemy of Empire is a possible author-portrait lead. CAIN man killed1972 aged33 rejected.
profiles.rights: No image selected; original credit and rights verification pending.
